sources.title: Tourism Visa – F5A
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Nigeria Immigration Service F5A page defines the ordinary tourism eVisa route, including its express ECOWAS and other waiver-agreement exceptions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of all countries except ECOWAS member States and other countries which Nigeria has entered into visa abolition/waiver agreements

sources.title: Nigeria Immigration Service Service Level Agreement, revised April 2026
sources.officialityEvidence: NIS's live April 2026 service-level agreement specifies the F5A online workflow, emailed certificate delivery and named country fee appendix.

sources.title: Nigerian Immigration Services e-Visa application
sources.officialityEvidence: The live NIS e-Visa portal is linked by the Nigeria Immigration Service's current F5A page and loads its nationality, visa-class and passport selectors through protected NIS configuration endpoints.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of ECOWAS member states and nationals of countries with visa abolition agreements ... are exempt from visa requirements.

unresolved.reason: Nigeria's current April 2026 Appendix I labels Georgia's single-entry row Gratis, while the F5A rule excludes any country with a visa-abolition or waiver agreement. Gratis does not say whether Georgia is waived, receives a zero-fee F5A certificate, or has another route. The live protected eVisa selector exposes no independently reproducible public Georgian eligibility result, and no current Georgian primary passport guidance directly identifies an ordinary tourist Nigerian eVisa route. The electronic certificate workflow alone therefore cannot establish GE eligibility.

Eswatini or Swaziland has no named current Appendix I single-entry row. Nigeria's F5A rule also reserves unenumerated bilateral waiver countries, so absence from a fee appendix or the public application form cannot establish eVisa eligibility. The protected live selector did not yield a reproducible public Eswatini nationality result, and no current Eswatini government passport guidance directly gives the Nigerian ordinary-tourist route.

Nigeria's current April 2026 Appendix I labels Afghanistan's single-entry row Gratis, which does not resolve the F5A waiver-agreement exception or identify an ordinary Afghan passport as eVisa-eligible. The public electronic-certificate workflow cannot supply this missing nationality result, and no current accessible Afghan primary source directly establishes a Nigerian ordinary-tourist eVisa, mission, waiver or other route. No Afghanistan parent-MFA material is used.
